RT by @NotWoofers: Hello everyone, I am starting a new fundraiser to help maintain and repair engineering equipment @LibertyUkraineF has already delivered to Ukraine with your aid. Donation link at the end of this post. Please read till the end, like, share and quote - it is very important for this fundraiser. Donations are tax deductible. Over the past 3 years, we have delivered more than 30 excavators, 40 heavy trucks, and loads of other engineering equipment such as cranes, augers, and off-road forklifts. 90% of the equipment we have delivered has performed exceptionally well, as we picked some of the most durable models. However, even the best equipment can't live forever, and the stress it's been put through on the battlefield shows. For example, one of the machines worked 12,000 hours over two years. That machine was a Yanmar VIO50 excavator that we bought, delivered, and serviced for $30,000. A new machine like this costs around $100,000. 12,000 machine hours is more than the expected lifetime of an excavator in this class. Today, this excavator returned to us for major repairs. I can't stress enough the importance of the work this machine performed. It served in the 43rd Artillery Brigade, building fortifications for PzH 2000 howitzers and digging trenches for drone pilots. It saved countless lives from drone threats and tens of millions of dollars in equipment by protecting critical assets. Today, we have a backlog of around 8 similar machines awaiting repairs. These machines have complex hydraulics, pins, and joints that require special equipment and expertise to repair. My goal has always been to deliver the best-value solutions for the least amount of funding. For example, a machine used to bore pin seats on an excavator costs around $15,000. We didn't have that kind of funding dedicated to repairs, so my brother @vaycartana built and programmed such a tool himself, and it cost us only $4,000. However, our ingenuity and desire to help Ukraine can only go so far without funding. We need parts, we need to pay for electricity, and we need to pay something to the workers who perform these repairs. This is back-breaking labor done under constant air raids, bombings, and air raid sirens. That's why I am asking you to donate to the fundraiser using the link at the end of this post. Our goal is to raise $30,000 to allow us to repair up to 6 excavators. Please share, quote repost, and like this post. It greatly helps visibility and directly impacts the battlefield. https://givebutter.com/engineering-equipment-repairs

After reading much of the commentary on the Mecca Agreement, I don't believe the superficial institutional similarities are sufficient to justify comparisons to NATO. And the agreement does not represent an anti-Western or anti-Eastern alignment. It is better understood as a regional framework designed to stabilize the immediate strategic environment. The agreement's unique combination of capabilities is what makes it stand out. Turkey contributes strong land forces and a mature defense industrial base; Saudi Arabia provides significant financial resources and air-power capability; and Pakistan adds a nuclear deterrent dimension. This combination gives the arrangement the potential to carry more strategic weight than many previous regional security initiatives. From a technical standpoint, the parties' power profiles are primarily complementary rather than redundant. As a result, the agreement's deterrence architecture appears more integrated and potentially scalable than comparable regional groupings. However, it would be premature to assign it a large geopolitical mission or to make assumptions about outcomes that have yet to occur. The agreement's long-term significance will be determined less by its headline ambitions than by its members' ability to translate complementary capabilities into sustained institutional and strategic cooperation.
